description: PyroTensor is a complete team of 6 UOM Engineering students building an AI-powered dashboard for the Flame in Freefall challenge. We're using machine learning and data visualization to make decades of microgravity combustion data easier to search, compare and interpret for fire safety in human space exploration. Our roster is full, so we're not recruiting, but we're happy to connect with other teams and mentors.

details:
What is EMBER?

Team PyroTensor developed EMBER (Exploration of Microgravity Burning through Experimental Research) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. EMBER is an SI (Super Intelligence)-powered web application designed to transform complex NASA combustion research data into useful insights for fire safety in space.

How EMBER works?

EMBER uses official NASA combustion research data to analyze scientific experiments and deliver useful insights into fire safety. Instead of simply answering questions like a traditional chatbot, EMBER connects users with relevant scientific experiments and ranks them according to how closely they match a specific problem.

The platform uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to retrieve information from its research database and generate answers supported by scientific citations. It also combines physics-based calculations with interactive visualizations to help users understand fire behavior.

Interactive Dashboard: Provides an overview of combustion research and fire safety information.

EMBER includes six main features:

  1. Cabin Configurator: Evaluates potential fire risks under different spacecraft cabin conditions.
  2. Flame Simulator: Visualizes flame behavior in normal gravity and microgravity.
  3. Ranking & Telemetry: Ranks scientific experiments by relevance and displays experimental measurements.
  4. Search Resources: Searches NASA combustion research and datasets, ranks relevant results, and provides access to original scientific sources.
  5. EMBER-SI: Answers scientific questions using relevant research evidence and citations.
  6. Live Telemetry: Processes simulated or externally supplied spacecraft sensor data in real time to calculate fire risks, identify contributing factors, visualize changing conditions, and match results with relevant NASA combustion experiments.

Technologies we use

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and WebGL2 for the interactive interface and flame visualization.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI for data processing, scientific calculations, and API development.
  • Database: PostgreSQL and pgvector for storing scientific data and supporting research retrieval.
  • SI Technologies: LangGraph, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector embeddings, and configurable language models, including Gemini.
  • Development Tools: Git, GitHub, Docker, and Visual Studio Code.

Creativity and Innovation

EMBER goes beyond a traditional research database or SI chatbot by combining scientific experiment ranking, physics-based fire risk analysis, interactive flame simulations, and evidence-supported SI explanations in one platform. Users can explore spacecraft conditions, visualize fire behavior in microgravity, and find relevant NASA research. This makes complex combustion science easier to understand and apply to real-world fire safety challenges.

Special Considerations

Our team focused on scientific accuracy, reliability, accessibility, user experience, and performance. We prioritized official NASA research data and scientific citations. We also designed interactive visualizations to simplify complex scientific concepts and ensured the platform could run on ordinary computers without specialized hardware.

Use of SI in EMBER

  • Claude Code: Debugging and code completion.
  • Google Antigravity: Error detection and troubleshooting.
  • OpenAI Codex: Code fixes and error handling.
